part.name: Stepped lever block with rounded head, through-bore, and underside pocket
part.description: Single solid part consisting of a large rounded-end head blending into a narrower rectangular arm. The arm contains an axial cylindrical bore that opens at the right end. An underside rectangular pocket provides clearance/weight reduction. External edges include large-radius rounds on the head and smaller rounds/chamfers near the right end.
part.symmetry_note: No full symmetry observed; geometry suggests partial bilateral intent but offsets/steps (underside pocket and end detailing) break strict symmetry.

Section.name: Rounded head / grip block
features included: Large rounded end-cap geometry (large corner radii)
Wide head footprint vs. narrower arm
Section.function intent: Provides a robust load introduction/handling region and a large bearing/stop surface area at the left end while smoothly blending stresses into the arm.
Section.physical behavior: Acts as a stiff mass distributing bending and shear loads from the arm into a thicker section; large radii reduce stress concentration at the head-to-arm transition and improve durability under cyclic bending.
Section.geometry: A wide rectangular block with large-radius external rounds and blended corners (mix of cylindrical and spherical/bspline patches). Leftmost end is a planar cap; underside includes a primary bottom plane and blended round transitions into side faces.
Section.location: Left side of the part (approx. x=0 to x=100), spanning the full width envelope (approx. y=200 to y=320) and full height (approx. z=-450 to z=-340).

Section.name: Main arm / beam body
features included: Narrower width than head (side planes at y=230 and y=294.336...)
Local chamfered/relief transitions near lower edges
Section.function intent: Connects the head to the right mounting/interface end, carrying bending/shear loads and providing a guided axial bore for a pin/fastener/shaft-like mating part.
Section.physical behavior: Behaves like a beam in bending and shear; the axial bore reduces weight and provides an interface while the remaining wall section resists loads. Flat side planes constrain lateral positioning in an assembly.
Section.geometry: Elongated rectangular prism-like arm with planar top, planar side faces, and a stepped/raised underside plane. Contains a cylindrical bore running along the x-direction beginning at the shoulder and continuing to the right end.
Section.location: Central length of the part (approx. x=100 to x=290), within the narrower y-span (approx. y=230 to y=294.336) and height between top plane z=-340 and underside step plane near z=-445.

Section.name: Right end interface / nose with bore exit and edge treatments
features included: Bore exit opening at the right end
Local chamfers and rounds near corners
Corner relief/fillet system (small-radius cylinders + conical transitions)
Local side step plane near y=250.211...
Section.function intent: Provides the primary mating/interface end where a pin/shaft can be inserted through the bore and where external faces can seat/abut against a mating component.
Section.physical behavior: Resists local bearing/contact stresses at the interface face and reduces stress concentrations via chamfers/rounds; maintains bore alignment and edge robustness against impacts.
Section.geometry: End block region with a planar end face at x=300 containing the bore opening, plus a combination of chamfer planes, cylindrical fillets, and conical transition faces around local corners/steps.
Section.location: Extreme right end of the part (approx. x=290 to x=300), around the bore centerline and local corner features.

Section.name: Underside rectangular pocket / recess
Section.function intent: Provides clearance for a mating feature, reduces mass, and/or creates space for fastener head/fixture engagement on the underside without changing the main external envelope.
Section.physical behavior: Removes material in a low-stress region (relative to outer fibers) to reduce weight while keeping outer beam surfaces continuous; pocket walls may act as locating boundaries if a mating protrusion enters.
Section.geometry: Rectangular prismatic cavity cut into the underside of the arm, bounded by planar faces: two x-direction side walls, a floor, a ceiling/opening boundary, and an end wall in y.
Section.location: Underside mid-arm region (approx. x=125 to x=168, y=230 to y=280, z between about -405 and -374).
